key_passages.text: A Dialogue between Narada and Bhakti (in a living form). Cessation of Bhakti's Suffering. Redemption of a Brahmana (Atmadeva)

Pariksit takes a vow of fasting till death and Suka pays a visit to him. Concentration on the gross and subtle forms of the Lord and the two types of Mukti (Liberation), viz. , Kramamukti or gradual Liberation and Sadyomukti or immediate Liberation

How to attain Liberation through the differentiation of Matter and Spirit. The process of the eightfold Yoga. Destiny of the souls departing from this world by the "Bright Path", the "Dark Path" and so on, and the superiority of Bhaktiyoga
Puranjana is reborn as a woman and attains liberation through the teaching of his friend, Avijhata. Bharata reborn for a second time in a Brahmana family

The messengers of Lord Visnu expound the Bhagavata Dharma (the cult of Devotion) and Ajamila ascends to the Lord's supreme Abode. An account of the birth of the Maruts (the forty-nine wind-gods). The procedure of observing the sacred vow of Purhsavana
